quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: Arithmetic error. Appendix A2 gives 348 vs 212, and 348/212 = 1.64, so StoneDB is about 64 percent higher, not 54.

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Causal claim stated as established fact. The only support is a README line describing the write path (A7); A1 says no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected. This is an inference from the vendor's description, not a measured cause.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: Unsupported generalisation. A1 says one machine with one NVMe SSD, no other hardware, and only batched fsync (every 1,000 writes). Per-write fsync was not tested, so nothing was measured on other hardware or durability settings.

quote: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
problem: Stated as a clear result, but A2 gives Marlin 417 [391-426] and StoneDB 402 [395-410] over 5 runs. The ranges overlap, so a 15-unit median gap is not shown to be a real difference. The report treats a comparable overlap as unresolved for the 100M test.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: Number contradicts the appendix. A3 gives KVLite's median p99 as 4.8 ms [4.5-5.2], not 4.2 ms. The StoneDB and Marlin figures match.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: Not supported. A1 says the longest single run was 6 minutes (5 measured), with no soak or multi-hour run. A5 covers only five one-minute readings. Short-run stability is presented as long-running sustainability.

quote: As for what the projects say about themselves, Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: Misstates the quoted source. A7 line 14 says Marlin is designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys. The report drops that qualifier and says 'generally', which makes the documentation's claim broader than what it says.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: Contradicted by the appendix. E1 says folios 31-34 are missing, and no entries are dated 12 Dec 1741 to 26 Jan 1742 (46 days). E2 and E3 show 212 entries over 716 days. The body itself says the editor found entries written up weeks later.

quote: The vestry responded by laying a rate for the poor, recorded on folio 38v.
problem: Causal link presented as fact. Q3 (fol. 38v) only records the rate and does not say it was a response to the mill or grain shortage. The mill passage is on fol. 39v, after the rate. This is the report's inference, not Wray's statement.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: Arithmetic error. E5(a) gives 52 in 1742 and 33 in 1741, a difference of 19, not 23.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: Contradicts E5(b), which says fever is named in 5 of the 29 death entries (cold or frost in 6, no cause in 18).

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. E5(b) shows cold or frost named in only 6 of 29 entries, and fever is named in 5 (Q6 also mentions fever). Against a rise of 19 burials, and with 18 entries naming no cause, 'alone' is not supported. The report itself says it does not reconstruct population.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Overstates the check. Q8 says the editor compared only nine of Wray's burial notices and did not check the rest. Nine of 29 death entries were checked, so the sample is not 'the entries' in general.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Misrepresents the source. Q5 (fol. 41r) says 'It is said by some', that Wray has not seen it with his own eyes, and that Mr. Hale says the barn is empty. Wray reports hearsay and does not assert it.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: Unsupported generalisation. E1 says the edition covers one parish and contains no records of any other parish and no comparative material (Ed. p. viii). Representativeness cannot be assessed from this evidence.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: Figures swapped. T2 says 48 not randomized = 31 ineligible (19 + 8 + 4) and 17 declined. Ineligibility, not declining, accounts for 31.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: Wrong percentage. 56/64 is 87.5%, which is what T2 reports, not 85.9%.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: No evidence. T1 and T7 say assessments were at baseline and week 8 only, with no assessment after week 8 and no follow-up planned. The program was still running at week 8, so persistence after it ended was not measured.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: Component attribution cannot be made. T1 and T7 (section 3.1) say the components were delivered together in a fixed sequence, no component was delivered alone, and the study does not test individual components.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: Not supported by T5. The median was 5 of 8 modules (IQR 3 to 8), only 11 of 32 (34.4%) completed all 8, and 8 of 32 completed 3 or fewer. No benchmark for 'high' is given.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: Overclaim. Protocol 7.4 says the study is not powered to estimate adverse event rates. There were only 32 app-arm participants, and events were self-reported. Collection also differed by arm (weekly check-in in the app arm, week 8 only in the control arm). Zero serious events in 32 does not show safety.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: Unsupported generalisation. This was a single-centre pilot of 64 night-shift nurses at one teaching hospital, with exploratory efficacy outcomes and no blinding. The results cannot be extended to shift workers generally.

quote: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: Extrapolation with no data. F3 says no specimen was tested below 3.0 kN, and testing stopped at 2,000,000 cycles with no test continued beyond runout. F2 says no statistical analysis was performed. Four runouts at 3.0 kN cannot show infinite life, and nothing below 3.0 kN was tested.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: Wrong number. F3 and the log show the shortest 4.0 kN failure was F4-04 at 1,238,000 cycles, not 1,138,000.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: In-sample count presented as a population probability. This is 3 failures of 4 specimens, one of them (F4-02) flagged as interrupted. F2 says no statistical analysis was performed, and the confidence interval on 3/4 is very wide. It should be reported as 3 of 4 observed.

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
problem: Arithmetic error. F3 gives 412,000, 366,000, 508,000 and 447,000, which sum to 1,733,000, so the mean is about 433,000, not 483,000.

quote: The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: Inference stated as established cause. S08 is the only lot B specimen, so lot is confounded with a single specimen. The lot B mill certificate is not on file, and the log says no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests on lot B are scheduled. The lot is a hypothesis only.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: No temperature data. F2 says all tests were at laboratory ambient (20.1 to 22.6 C) and none at other temperatures. REQ-EN-003 requires -30 C to +50 C.

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: Overstated. TP-221 says the method was 'adapted from' ASTM E466 with listed deviations: 4 specimens per level against a plan target of 6, and load frame alignment not verified. 'In accordance with' is not accurate.
